analysis:
Examined the documentation changes in docs/architecture/inference.md (the visible tail covers MiMo, Flint, Qwen4 and Bonsai text). The only changed line in the file's range map is the `stop` row at line 1866, which now describes per-request reasoning and tool-call stop scoping. That row is outside the supplied text units, but the patch excerpt is complete. The doc change is descriptive only and alters no controls.

EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift adds an optional `stopStringScope` parameter (default nil) to `runPump` and `pump`. It forwards the parameter into `matchedStopSequence(..., scope:)`, which feeds only `usageSignal.record(matchedStopSequence:)`. Nothing is added to the wire, the logs or telemetry. No request text is introduced into telemetry, and the existing privacy comments on the telemetry emitters are untouched. The parameter affects only replay of matched-stop metadata for usage reporting. Decrypted prompts, E2E encryption, attestation and the cache-storage paths (T-041) are untouched. KV reservation release, receipt completion and retirement ordering in the pump are unchanged.

The mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves from 2beb401 to 5ffbb80. The submodule content is not supplied, so its security effect (the CBv2StopStringScope type, the engine stop-holdback and the SDK changes in general) cannot be verified here. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

Open integration questions: (1) whether call sites in the other bridge files (the submission path and EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift) pass the scope consistently, and whether `matchedStopSequence` accepts the new `scope:` argument. A mismatch would be a compile or behavior issue, not a security one. (2) What the bumped submodule changes in the inference engine, the prefix cache and the memory ledger. A reviewer with access to the submodule diff should check it. I set needs_deeper_review for the unreviewed submodule bump only.
